pages.lesson:
LESSON: READING 6.2.1 INTENSIVE READING COMPREHENSION DIALOGUES

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 6
Topic 6.2: Reading 6.2.1 Intensive Reading Comprehension Dialogues

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading 6.2.1 Intensive Reading Comprehension Dialogues. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How can we guess the meaning of words?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. use contextual clues to infer the meaning of words from a text
2. respond to direct and inferential questions for comprehension

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: READING 6.2.1 INTENSIVE READING COMPREHENSION DIALOGUES
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE · Grade: Grade 5
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Reading 6.2.1 Intensive Reading Comprehension Dialogues helps you succeed in ENGLISH LANGUAGE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: READING 6.2.1 INTENSIVE READING COMPREHENSION DIALOGUES
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Use contextual clues to infer the meaning of words from a text

What this means
In this part you learn to use contextual clues to infer the meaning of words from a text. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use contextual clues to infer the meaning of words from a text.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 6.2.1 Intensive Reading Comprehension Dialogues”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use contextual clues to infer the meaning of words from a text. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Respond to direct and inferential questions for comprehension

What this means
In this part you learn to respond to direct and inferential questions for comprehension. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: respond to direct and inferential questions for comprehension.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 6.2.1 Intensive Reading Comprehension Dialogues to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can respond to direct and inferential questions for comprehension. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Reading 6.2.1 Intensive Reading Comprehension Dialogues is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 6.2.1 Intensive Reading Comprehension Dialogues”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: use contextual clues to infer the meaning of words from a text)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 6.2.1 Intensive Reading Comprehension Dialogues to a partner. (skill: respond to direct and inferential questions for comprehension)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Reading 6.2.1 Intensive Reading Comprehension Dialogues to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: use contextual clues to infer the meaning of words from a text.
3. Practise this skill: respond to direct and inferential questions for comprehension.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Reading 6.2.1 Intensive Reading Comprehension Dialogues from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Reading 6.2.1 Intensive Reading Comprehension Dialogues: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 5 learner study Reading 6.2.1 Intensive Reading Comprehension Dialogues?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How can we guess the meaning of words?
2. What makes you a good reader?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Reading 6.2.1 Intensive Reading Comprehension Dialogues means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: use contextual clues to infer the meaning of words from a text.
5. Be able to: respond to direct and inferential questions for comprehension.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
